title: Public policy and enforceability
summary: Public-policy rules can limit enforcement of an agreement because of interests the law protects beyond the parties’ private exchange.
notes:
Identify the policy’s source and the connection between that policy and the promise being enforced. A licensing violation, illegal performance, or restraint on work may present different questions. Blossom Farm examines the consequences of unlawful conduct connected with a sale; X.L.O. considers an agreement connected with an alleged antitrust violation. The existence of wrongdoing does not automatically answer which party may enforce which obligation or obtain restitution.

Hassler addresses an overbroad employment restraint and whether a court should rewrite it. The supplementary FTC materials concern a dated federal rule-removal history, not a conclusion that every private noncompete is valid. State statutes and judicial standards remain separate questions. Policy analysis should identify the protected interest, the effect of enforcement or nonenforcement, and the remedy appropriate to the case.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.public-policy: The law can limit bargains for reasons extending beyond private assent.
